messages.author: 782ed6ec348dba9b
messages.subject: Fine tuning CSS
parts:
I have an app where I am posting NHL scores

data <- reactive({

# loop through data
#construct data.frame "score"

#  take elements from this dataframe 
 line <- data.frame(NHL = paste0(score[1,1]," ",score[1,2],"-",score[2,2]," ",score[2,1]," ",score[1,3]," ",score[2,3]))

# combine lines

return(allLines)

}

    output$nhl <- renderTable({
      data()
    },include.rownames=FALSE)

The output looks like this

 Boston 3-4 NY Rangers Final OT
 Chicago 0-2 Detroit Final 
San Jose 0-3 Los Angeles Final

I want to change the look via CSS
I can make global changes 
e.g
div #nhl {
  font-weight: bold;
}

but am looking to fine tune by ,say, bolding the winning team, having different background for scores etc.
so presumably want to add span(s) in the
line <- data.frame(NHL = paste0(score[1,1]," ",score[1,2],"-",score[2,2]," ",score[2,1]," ",score[1,3]," ",score[2,3]))
but am having trouble getting it to work

Any help appreciated

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Fine tuning CSS
parts: I would recommend using the hwriter package (http://www.ebi.ac.uk/~gpau/hwriter/), which allows finer control for html tables. You can then use renderText along with htmlOutput to display your table. I will cook up a simple example when I find time, but it is fairly straightforward once you get a hang of how hwriter works.

 Looking forward to your example though I know you have a lot on with rCharts etc.
cheers
Andrew

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Fine tuning CSS
parts:
Here is a sample gist

runGist('https://gist.github.com/ramnathv/5649899')

The idea is to create a data frame with the classes you want to inject, and pass it to hwrite. I am injecting styles using UI.R, but ideally you would want to stick it into a css file.

Let me know if this helps.
